claims.text: The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy has no pre-existing secondary phases that contribute to self-lubrication.
The proposed intervention adds 5 wt% Ag to CoCrFeMnNi.
An optimized aging treatment after Ag addition will form uniformly distributed nanoscale Ag precipitates.
The optimized aging treatment will stabilize the nanoscale Ag precipitates and prevent their coarsening.
The nanoscale Ag precipitates will migrate to the sliding interface during wear.
Ag arriving at the sliding interface will coalesce into a continuous Ag-rich tribofilm.
The Ag-rich tribofilm will be lubricious and have low shear strength.
The Ag-rich tribofilm will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact.
Minimizing direct metal-to-metal contact through the Ag-rich film will reduce the coefficient of friction.
Minimizing direct metal-to-metal contact through the Ag-rich film will reduce wear rate.
The Ag-modified and aged alloy will retain its friction- and wear-reduction effect from room temperature to approximately 500 degrees Celsius.
Relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi, the Ag-modified and aged alloy will exhibit an approximately 30% lower coefficient of friction.
Relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi, the Ag-modified and aged alloy will exhibit a significant decrease in wear rate.
Untreated CoCrFeMnNi has higher friction than the proposed Ag-modified and aged alloy under similar test conditions.
Untreated CoCrFeMnNi has a higher wear rate than the proposed Ag-modified and aged alloy under similar test conditions.
Suboptimal aging parameters may cause Ag precipitate coarsening and limit the intervention's efficacy.
Service-induced unwanted phase transformations may limit the intervention's efficacy.
Maintaining nanoscale precipitate size and distribution will provide durable tribological performance across the targeted temperature range.
